title: OpenAI cuts GPT-6 Sol and Luna prices in half, landing same day as Claude Opus 5.5
subtitle: OpenAI shipped GPT-6 Sol at $2/$10 per million tokens and Luna at $0.10/$0.50 — roughly 50% below the prior 5.6 tier and framed as permanent — 90 minutes after Anthropic released Claude Opus 5.5.
author: AESOP AI Engine
body: OpenAI released GPT-6 Sol and GPT-6 Luna on September 22, 2026, priced at $2 per million input tokens and $10 per million output tokens for Sol, and $0.10/$0.50 for Luna. Cached input drops to 10% of the input price on both. OpenAI framed the change as permanent, not promotional, and said improvements in caching and inference let it serve the models at lower cost. The announcement landed roughly 90 minutes after Anthropic released Claude Opus 5.5 at $4/$20 — putting Sol at exactly half of Opus 5.5's per-token cost on both dimensions.

Same-day, tit-for-tat pricing between the two labs is new. Both are also claiming higher benchmark scores than their prior flagships, so the effective cost-per-task drop is bigger than the sticker prices imply. Anthropic said Opus 5.5 costs about 40% less to run on typical workloads because it also uses fewer tokens per task. The pressure is mechanical — reasoning-tier models were burning cash at the token counts real agentic use cases require, and both labs need those use cases to work economically before the tier below them commoditizes further.

This is the third round of coordinated price movement since April 2026. Anthropic priced Claude Opus 5 at half of Opus 4.8. OpenAI answered with GPT-5.6 Luna at an 80% cut. Anthropic responded with Sonnet 5 tokenizer changes that lowered inference costs on typical workloads. Chinese labs led by DeepSeek and Zhipu have run below both since summer. The pattern signals that the industry expects agentic, long-horizon workloads to become the volume driver — and that per-token pricing is being reset for that world, not for chat.

Takeaway for learners — when two competitors match each other's price cut within 90 minutes, it means capacity and demand have stabilized enough that price is now the lever they can pull without losing money. Watch which workloads move first — agentic coding, long-context research assistants, and multi-step data pipelines get economical at these prices in a way they weren't at $20 per million output tokens. If you have been holding off on a project that needs a frontier model, the cost math has shifted twice this month.
